column1: # lean-twins.tsv — THE RUST-TWIN REGRESSION GUARD that scripts/ci-invariants.sh enforces.
# A "twin" = a Rust function that DECIDES accept/admit/conserve/finalize where a
# Lean `@[export]` proves the same property, so the two can DRIFT. The asset-inflation
# CRITICAL *was* the per-asset-conservation twin drifting. The twin-deletion campaign
# (docs/TWIN-DELETION-MAP-2026-07-23.md) routed all 11 live decisions through the proven
# `@[export]` (fail-CLOSED when absent) and left each Rust sibling only under `#[cfg(test)]`
# as a differential mirror. This registry is the STRUCTURAL CANARY that keeps it that way.
# It is a heuristic grep-lint (v1), NOT a theorem: it reads the source at HEAD and asserts
# the shape of each twin site is intact. It cannot prove semantic equivalence — it prevents
# the KNOWN regressions (a native/rust/mirror sibling re-appearing on the live path, or the
# route-through to Lean being ripped out and the decision inlined in Rust).
# COLUMNS (tab-separated; blank lines and #-comments ignored):
#   guard   one of:
#     route    -> `pattern` MUST be present in `file` (the live decider still calls the
#                 verified export / fail-closed disposition; if it vanishes, a twin was inlined)
#     forbid   -> `pattern` MUST NOT be present in `file` (a deleted Rust twin decider reappeared)
#     cfgtest  -> `fn <pattern>` in `file` MUST be `#[cfg(test)]`-gated (the differential
#                 sibling may exist, but only in test builds — never on a live path)
#   file      the source file that owns the live decision (FATAL if it moved — re-point the row)
#   pattern   a regex (route/forbid) or a bare fn name (cfgtest)
#   note      one line — which twin (# from the map) and what the guard protects
# TO EXTEND (a new twin, or a new @[export] to guard): add rows. To enumerate the export
# surface this guards, see docs/CI-INVARIANTS.md (the `verified_*`/`shadow_*` FFI bridges).
# guard

column1: # ── twin#13's FIVE SIBLING PQ DIRECTIONS — guarded HERE, deliberately NOT in invariant 6 ───────
# MEASURED (2026-07-25), not assumed: rows registering the sibling sites in `gate-dataflow.tsv` with
# `guard_unaudited_fallback` as the declared discriminator are RED — 4 of 5 print "the row DECLARES
# the carve-out but the gate-absent path has NO refusal on the non-exempt arm". They are not
# fail-OPEN; the refusal is `audit::refuse_unaudited(..) -> !`, a DIVERGING call in ANOTHER FILE, and
# `gate-dataflow.py` resolves helpers only within the same file and has no notion of `!`. The fifth
# (`MlDsaKey::try_sign`) prints PASS on a `return None` inlined out of `decode_hex` — i.e. the one
# green would have been DECORATION. Registering rows that are red-for-the-wrong-reason (or green for
# the wrong reason) would make invariant 6 lie in both directions, so the sibling coverage is these
# structural route rows plus the `dregg-pq` falsifier rows in `falsifiers.tsv`.
route
